items.actClause: AN ACT to amend chapter 504 of the laws of 2009 amending the retirement and social security law and other laws relating to establishing police and fire retirement provisions, in relation to persons joining a public retirement system on or after July 1, 2009 and before January 10, 2010
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S7174

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend chapter 504 of the laws of 2009 amending the
retirement and social security law and other laws relating to
establishing police and fire retirement provisions, in relation to
persons joining a public retirement system on or after July 1, 2009
and before January 10, 2010

 PURPOSE :

To allow any member of the New York State and Local Police and Fire
Retirement System who joined pursuant to Article 14 of the Retirement
and Social Security Law to elect to have his or her benefits
recalculated pursuant to Article 22.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1 of this bill amends Section B of Part A of Chapter 504 of
the Laws of 2009 to provide that any member of the New York State and
Local Police and Fire Retirement System who joined pursuant to Article
14 may elect to have his or her retirement benefits recalculated
pursuant to Article 22. Additionally, any affected member shall be
allowed to elect any noncontributory plan that would have been
available to him or her if he or she been covered by Article 22
beginning on July 1, 2009 and ending before January 10, 2010.

Section 2 of this bill provides that any member wishing to make an
election to Article 22 must do so within 180 days of the effective
date of this Chapter and such election must be made on a form provided
by the State Comptroller.

Section 3 of this bill provides that this act shall take effect
immediately.

 EXISTING LAW :

Retirement and Social Security Law section 1205 provided members of
the New York State and Local Police and Fire Retirement System who
joined pursuant to Article 14 of the Retirement and Social Security
Law with the opportunity to elect to have their benefits recalculated
pursuant to Article 22. The period to make this election ended in
early April 2010.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Over the past few years, there have been an increasing number of
requests by members to reopen the election provided by Retirement and
Social Security Law submitted in accordance with Senate Rule VI. Sec 1
section 1205. This option was created as part of Tier V. At that time,
there were mixed reports regarding whether Tier V was beneficial to
members. Reopening this option is important because as the years have
gone by, members who failed opt into Article 22 for whatever reason,
whether it be confusion regarding what the election meant or the
differences between Articles 14 and 22, may wish to make such an
election.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New bill

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

See the fiscal note attached to the bill.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.

A.actClause: AN ACT to amend chapter 504 of the laws of 2009 amending the retirement and social security law and other laws relating to establishing police and fire retirement provisions, in relation to persons joining a public retirement system on or after July 1, 2009 and before January 10, 2010
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S7174A

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend chapter 504 of the laws of 2009 amending the
retirement and social security law and other laws relating to
establishing police and fire retirement provisions, in relation to
persons joining a public retirement system on or after July 1, 2009
and before January 10, 2010

 PURPOSE :

After the veto of the New York State Police & Fire Retirement system
Tier II, there was a period from July 1st, 2009 through January 10th,
2010 that placed newly hired police officers and firefighters in the
Tier III system. Once the enactment of Tier V took effect, it allowed
these members the ability to opt in to Tier V. This option expired in
2010. There are now situations where members are being hired as police
officers and fire fighters, who had previous credit in the retirement
system and have been placed in the tier that coincides with their
original starting date in the pension system. The members who started
with the retirement system during the above mentioned period can only
be placed back in Tier III, since the option to go into Tier V has
expired. If this bill is enacted, the member will have the option to
be placed into the Tier V system; the same option the members
originally had in 2010.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

This bill would amend the Retirement and Social Security Law to allow
certain members the ability to establish Tier V benefits.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Members who are hired as public employees and placed into the
retirement system have the right to obtain the benefits and privileges
of the original date of entry into the system. In some instances, when
a member moves from one public employment career to another, it
changes the pension tier that they were originally placed in. The
Constitution, which protects any diminishment of pension rights,
allows the member to use his or her original starting date. The
members that use the original starting dates of June 30th, 2009
through January 10th 2010 can only be placed in Tier III because
during that period a new pension tier to replace Tier II had yet to be
developed. Once Tier V came into existence, the members at that time
were allowed to opt in to Tier V. This bill would create the same
option. Furthermore, placing these members into Tier V rather than
Tier III would be a cost savings to both the State and participating
municipalities because the contribution rate for the Tier III plan is
greater than that of Tier V.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

The option this bill allows was available in 2010.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

See The Bill.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately
